instruction: Retrieve the invoice PDF from Google Drive and extract its data into a LibreOffice Calc spreadsheet saved as 'invoice.xlsx' on the Desktop. Ensure the extracted data has at least 3 columns.

metadata.explanation: This task requires extracting invoice data with at least 3 columns of information. The evaluator counts the number of non-empty columns in the xlsx file.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification coverage: Evaluator only checks column count (structural property) but doesn't verify that data was actually extracted from the invoice PDF
Missing semantic verification: Instruction requires 'extract its data' but evaluator cannot distinguish between meaningful invoice data vs random/garbage data with 3 columns
No source verification: Doesn't verify that data came from Google Drive or that source was an invoice PDF - could pass if user manually creates any 3-column xlsx file
Structural check masquerading as semantic verification: The core task is PDF data extraction, but the evaluator only checks file format/structure
Logic will pass false positives: A completely empty extraction with 3 column headers, or random data in 3 columns, would incorrectly pass the evaluation
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add verification of actual invoice content: Check for presence of invoice-specific data (e.g., amounts, dates, line items, invoice number) to ensure meaningful extraction occurred
Add sample-based content verification: Compare a few cells with expected invoice data patterns or verify that numeric columns contain plausible invoice amounts
Consider adding row count verification: Invoices typically have multiple line items, so checking minimum row count (e.g., >= 2-3 rows) would help verify actual data extraction
Alternative: If only structural check is desired, simplify the instruction to 'Create an xlsx file with at least 3 columns' to match what evaluator actually verifies
